To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed and implemented an accurate and efficient numerical method for the FUS simulation during respiratory motion of abdominal targets and that we have incorporated this method into a simulation application for clinical treatment planning.

we have developed a novel simulation method for FUS treatments during motion, that allows for motion discontinuity, e.g., sliding of the liver, and that is computationally highly efficient and can therefore be used in clinical applications.

we present a method for fast numerical simulation of focused ultrasound treatments during respiratory motion, that is implemented completely on the graphics card, that can simulate real patient cases, and that is fast enough to be used in clinical practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel simulation methods for FUS treatments during motion.
the development and implementation of a novel numerical method for the fast and accurate simulation of focused ultrasound (FUS)-based therapies during respiratory organ motion.
the development of a novel simulation framework for the simulation of ultrasound treatments during respiratory motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented methods are highly efficient and accurate and thus, bear the potential for clinical use.
the method is a step toward a clinically applicable FUS treatment planning and execution tool for moving organs.
the presented methods bear the potential for the clinical application of FUS to moving organs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel numerical simulation approach for FUS treatments of moving organs.
we have developed a simulation method that can be used for the treatment planning of FUS for liver tumors during respiration, which has been a major challenge for FUS in the past.
we have developed a fast numerical simulation approach for FUS treatments of moving organs, and we have integrated the method into a clinical application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simulation method that is fast enough to allow for real-time simulation of a treatment can also be highly accurate.
a computationally efficient simulation of FUS treatments is possible for the first time, which allows for the clinical application.
the presented simulation method allows to simulate the heating effects of FUS during motion of the target organ.
